title: Stargazing in Berlin - FAQ
subtitle: Where to look through a telescope in Berlin this autumn, what it costs, and how to pick the right night.

items.q: Where can I look through a telescope in Berlin?
items.a: At the **Archenhold Observatory in Treptower Park** and the **Wilhelm-Foerster Observatory on the Insulaner in Schöneberg**. Both run public evening sessions called Nacht auf der Sternwarte from October to December.

items.q: How much does an observatory night in Berlin cost?
items.a: **€12, or €8 reduced** for under-18s, pupils, students and trainees. A family ticket for two adults and up to three children costs €31.50 and is sold only at the box office or by phone.

items.q: When are the observatories open at night?
items.a: **Archenhold opens Thursday, Friday and Saturday; Wilhelm-Foerster opens Friday and Saturday.** Both have sessions at 20:00 and 22:00, each lasting 90 minutes.

items.q: Are the telescope sessions in English?
items.a: **No, they are hosted in German.** The English options are the dome shows Starry Night and Encounters in the Milky Way at the Archenhold Observatory and the Zeiss-Großplanetarium.

items.q: What happens if it is cloudy?
items.a: **The session still runs.** At the Archenhold Observatory the group moves into the planetarium or the Einstein-Saal and sees the sky projected instead.

items.q: Can children go to the observatory at night?
items.a: The evening sessions are for ages 12 and up. From **30 October, both observatories add Sternenkieker sessions at 18:00 on Fridays and Saturdays for children from 8**, at the same price.

items.q: When is the best time to see Saturn from Berlin this autumn?
items.a: **Saturn is at opposition on 4 October.** In October book the 22:00 session, when it stands about 30 degrees high; from November it is highest in the south at 20:00.
